items.text: A new standing-watch development. Wyoming's Select Committee on Gaming has drafted bill 27LSO-0098, which would ban online casinos and sweepstakes games by folding them into the state's existing professional gambling statute, already a felony carrying up to three years in prison. The committee sent the draft to the Legislature's Management Council, which will decide whether to sponsor it for the 2027 session at a meeting expected in mid to late November or early December. A competing draft, 27LSO-0200, which would have legalized and regulated sweepstakes gaming with a 21 and over age limit, failed to advance at the committee's most recent meeting. This is separate from Wyoming's existing regulated skill game program under W.S. 11-25-301 et seq., whose tax rate, machine limit, wager cap and payout cap remain unchanged.

items.text: The legislative feed refreshed, generated at 16:35 UTC on October 19, 2026, the first new scan since the October 16 run already reported on this page. Totals moved to 313 matching bills, 86 primary and 227 secondary, with five new records, one of them primary, and no changed records. The new primary record is Virginia Senate Bill 579, covered as its own item below. Of the four new secondary records, Virginia House Bill 271 is also reported separately below because it matches strongly on skill game language even though the feed classifies it as secondary tier. The other three are not on topic: Massachusetts House Bill 5501, the recurring fiscal year 2027 budget bill that has cycled in and out of the matched set since early October on the incidental phrase amusement device; Ohio Senate Bill 479, introduced October 13, which would classify betting on elections as prohibited gambling and matches only on the incidental phrases amusement machine and sweepstakes; and Virginia Senate Bill 604, a charitable bingo bill for age restricted communities that matches only on the incidental phrase electronic gaming device.

Virginia Senate Bill 579 would add operating, conducting or promoting an online sweepstakes game to the state's definition of illegal gambling. It defines an online sweepstakes game as an internet or mobile game that uses a dual currency system letting a player exchange one currency for a prize, cash or cash equivalent and that simulates casino style gaming such as slot machines, video poker, table games or sports betting, and it sets a civil penalty of not less than 10,000 dollars and not more than 100,000 dollars per violation. LegiScan's record shows the bill carried over from the prior session into the 2027 regular session, with a last action of continued from last session dated July 21, 2026, and no floor or committee action yet in the new session. This bill was not previously reported on this page.

items.text: Virginia House Bill 271 would establish a Virginia Gaming Commission as an independent agency to oversee and regulate all forms of legal gambling in the commonwealth except the state lottery, with its own eligibility rules for commissioners and board members and a provision to transfer staff from existing gaming agencies. Like Senate Bill 579, LegiScan shows this bill continued from the prior session into the 2027 regular session, with a last action dated July 21, 2026, and no floor or committee action yet in the new session. Similar proposals for a Virginia gaming commission have circulated since at least January 2026 without passing.

The Pennsylvania Supreme Court's 120 day stay on its June 15 ruling that skill games are slot machines expired at the close of October 13, 2026. State Police guidance says machines outside Pennsylvania Gaming Control Board licensed locations are now unlawful and subject to immediate seizure, criminal prosecution under Section 5513 of the Crimes Code, asset forfeiture and liquor license citations, with no grace period beyond October 14. No tax or extension bill passed either chamber before the deadline. Reporting attributes this in part to the state constitution's three day rule, which requires a bill to be considered on three separate days in each chamber with no emergency exception, leaving no time to act after the court denied the final extension petition on October 9. The General Assembly does not return until October 19, five days into enforcement.

Attorney General Dave Sunday said his office does not want to see searches and seizures at storefronts, bars, social clubs and restaurants but will act in accordance with the law. His office and State Police put the installed base at roughly 70,000 machines across four to six brands, with Pace-O-Matic's Pennsylvania Skill brand accounting for about 20,000 of them. Pace-O-Matic said communities across the state are now facing the consequences of the impasse and does not expect legislative action before the November election. Some locations, including a Dauphin County VFW post and other clubs and bars, have already removed their machines voluntarily; distributor Miele Manufacturing told host locations last week it would power down units at its next collection round, which the attorney general's office has said does not by itself satisfy the law.

Two more sweepstakes platforms moved to restrict Oklahoma ahead of the November 1 effective date, beyond the Pulsz Gold Coin only restriction already reported. Modo told players by email that Oklahoma purchases of Gold Coin packages with promotional Sweeps Coin stopped October 1, with Sweeps Coin play and redemption continuing only through October 31 and Gold Coin only play surviving afterward. Stake.us told an Oklahoma player it will no longer be available to Oklahoma players starting October 30, though redemption of existing balances appeared to remain open for now. No new enforcement guidance from Attorney General Gentner Drummond's office or state gaming authorities and no legal challenge to the statute were found this week.

entries.headline: Pennsylvania State Police tell businesses to physically remove skill games before 13 October, and say unplugging them is not compliance.

items.text: The Pennsylvania State Police issued compliance guidance on 9 September 2026 ahead of the stay expiring. It tells establishments to remove skill game machines now and states that simply powering off an otherwise operable machine or unplugging it is not sufficient to comply with the law. From 14 October, PSP says machines, associated equipment and the money associated with their operation are subject to seizure and forfeiture, and criminal charges may follow. The release directs establishments to contact their distributor or vendor to arrange removal, and says that if a vendor refuses, the establishment is encouraged to contact PSP for help removing the machines.

Rep. Brad Roae of Crawford and Erie counties filed a co-sponsorship memo on Monday 14 September 2026 for legislation that would push the enforcement deadline from 13 October 2026 to 13 April 2027, temporarily legalizing the machines without taxing them while a permanent framework is negotiated. No bill number has appeared and the legislative feed shows no new Pennsylvania bill introduced as of 19 September, so this remains a memo rather than filed legislation.

Rep. Russ Diamond announced a two bill package on 2 September 2026 that puts detail behind his 20 percent number, and the detail matters more than the rate for anyone placing machines. It would cap locations at five machines, limit eligibility to clubs, bars and restaurants holding liquor licenses plus qualified truck stops, and exclude convenience stores, gas stations and dedicated skill game parlors. It would also cut the casino slot rate to 49.9 percent and route revenue to property tax relief. Diamond said on 9 September the bills were likely to be introduced within the week; they have not appeared in the feed.

No tax proposal has passed either chamber. The House and Senate each have about six voting days scheduled between 28 September and 7 October, which is the whole runway before the stay expires. Two figures in circulation conflict and are worth pinning down before anyone relies on them: the Senate Republican rate is reported as 35 percent in some coverage and 36 percent in other coverage, and the installed base is given as roughly 70,000 devices in court and law enforcement coverage against an industry estimate of about 50,000 machines.

County prosecutors are positioning for the handover. The Bucks County District Attorney's office said on 18 September 2026 that it will consult with the State Police but that troopers are leading enforcement, with the county prosecuting cases referred to it. No grace period beyond 13 October has been described by any Pennsylvania agency so far.

Attorney General Letitia James announced on 9 September 2026 that VGW Holdings, which runs Chumba Casino, Global Poker and LuckyLand Slots, will pay 8 million dollars in disgorgement, penalties and costs and must stop offering sweeps coin play in New York. The office alleged that coins presented as free were in practice obtained at roughly one coin per dollar spent, which is the same characterization other attorneys general have used against the dual currency model.

The North Carolina Supreme Court heard argument on 9 September 2026 in No Limit Games v. Sheriff of Robeson County, on whether video sweepstakes terminals fall foul of the state ban where chance determines the prize even if the game itself is skill based. The Court of Appeals ruled against the operator two to one in December 2024. No decision has issued and one could land at any time. One outlet dated the argument 11 September, which is a Friday and inconsistent with the court's sitting, so 9 September is the date carried here.

items.text: The Pennsylvania Supreme Court held on 15 June 2026 that skill games are slot machines under the Gaming Act and Crimes Code, and stayed enforcement for 120 days to let the legislature act. Five tax proposals are competing: 52 percent from the Shapiro administration, 35 percent from Senate Republicans, 20 percent from Rep. Russ Diamond, 16 percent from Sen. Yaw, and a flat 500 dollars per unit per month from Sens. Yaw and Williams. No proposal had passed as of this entry.

Governor Stitt vetoed the dual-currency sweepstakes ban on 7 May 2026 and the legislature overrode him on 15 May, Senate 34 to 10 and House 68 to 19. The ban takes effect 1 November 2026. Liability reaches past the operator to payment processors, geolocation providers, gaming suppliers, platform providers and media affiliates. Tribal gaming under IGRA and charitable gaming are exempt. Operators are lawfully live until the effective date.

Signed by Governor Reynolds and effective 1 July 2026, giving the Iowa Racing and Gaming Commission authority to issue cease-and-desist orders against unlicensed operators, reaching dual-currency sweepstakes products. High 5 Casino and Baba Casino exited before the effective date; Stake.us, WOW Vegas and Chumba Casino did not. No enforcement action has been reported since, which is the thing to watch.
